Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 38, verse 10–12:

﴿Or do they have dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them?﴾ That is: they do not have that. ﴿Then let them ascend by means (asbab)﴾ That is: if they claim any part of that, then let them climb by the means that bring them to the sky, and let them bring down revelation from it to whomever they choose. Mujahid and Qatadah said: By the asbab is meant the gates of the sky and its paths from one heaven to another, and whatever brings you to something by a gate or a path is its sabab (means). This is a command of rebuke and of rendering them powerless.

﴿A host, there, defeated, of the factions﴾ That is: these who make this claim are a host there, and "ma" is a redundant particle (silah). ﴿Defeated (mahzum)﴾ meaning overcome, ﴿of the factions (al-ahzab)﴾ That is: among the total of the hosts, meaning the Quraysh.

Qatadah said: Allah the Exalted informed His Prophet ﷺ, while he was in Makkah, that He would defeat the host of the polytheists, and He said: ﴿The host will be routed and they will turn their backs﴾ [al-Qamar: 45], and its interpretation came on the day of Badr [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 23/130, and al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/147 also attributed it to Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim.]]. "There" is an indication of Badr and their places of slaughter. "Of the factions" means: of the total of the factions, that is, they are among the past generations who banded together and gathered against the prophets with denial, so they were subdued and destroyed. Then He said, consoling His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Before them denied the people of Noah, and ʿAd, and Pharaoh of the stakes (dhu al-awtad)﴾. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 38, verses 13–15:

﴿And Thamud, and the people of Lot, and the companions of the Thicket. Those are the confederates.﴾ Those who banded together against the prophets. Thus He informed that the polytheists of Quraysh are a faction of these confederates.

﴿And these [people of Makkah] await not but one blast,﴾ meaning: they await, ﴿and there is no delay for it.﴾ "Blast" is the blowing of the Trumpet. ﴿Without any reprieve (fawaq)﴾: Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "fuwaq" with a ḍammah on the fa', while the others read it with a fatḥah, and both are dialects: the fatḥah is the dialect of Quraysh, and the ḍammah is the dialect of Tamim.

Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: "from return," meaning that the sound is not returned so that it would have a return.

Mujahid said: "a respite." Al-Dahhak said: "a second chance," that is, deferment and turning back.

The meaning is: that cry, which is the appointed time of their punishment, when it comes, will not be turned back nor deferred.

Some scholars distinguished between the fatḥah and the ḍammah. Al-Farra' and Abu 'Ubaydah said: the fatḥah means rest and recovery, like "jawab" from "ijabah"; they took it to mean the recovery of the sick from his illness. And "fuwaq" with a ḍammah is the interval between two milkings, which is when a she-camel is milked and then left for a while until the milk gathers; what lies between the two milkings is "fuwaq," meaning that the punishment does not give them respite for that length of time. [[See: Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra': 3/400; Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubaydah: 2/179.]]

It was also said: both of them are likewise borrowed from the meaning of return, because the milk returns to the udder between the two milkings, and the recovery of the sick is his return to health.

Then Allah revealed to Dawud in his dream that he should kill the one against whom the complaint was made. He said: "This is a dream, and I will not hasten until I verify it." Then He revealed to him a second time, and he did not act. Then Allah revealed to him a third time that he should kill him or the punishment would come to him. Dawud sent for him and said: "Allah has revealed to me that I should kill you." The man said: "You will kill me without proof?" Dawud said: "Yes, by Allah, I will carry out the command of Allah concerning you." When the man realized that he would be killed, he said: "Do not hasten until I inform you. **The Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 38, Verse 21**

His saying, Exalted and Majestic is He: ﴿Has the news of the adversaries reached you, when they climbed over the prayer chamber?﴾ ] [[The words in the parentheses are missing from manuscript "B".]] This verse is part of the account of the trial of Dawud (David), peace be upon him. The scholars of tafsir (Qur'anic exegesis) differed, in the reports about the prophets, peace be upon them, concerning its cause.

Some people said: The cause of this was that he, peace be upon him, once wished for the rank of Ibrahim (Abraham), Ishaq (Isaac) and Ya'qub (Jacob). He asked his Lord to test him as He had tested them, and to give him the same bounty He had given them.

Al-Suddi, al-Kalbi and Muqatil reported, from their shaykhs, with the narrations of some of them mixed into others, that they said: Dawud had divided time into three days: a day on which he judged between people, a day on which he withdrew to worship his Lord, and a day for his wives and his affairs. He found in the books he read the excellence of Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qub. He said: "O Lord, I see all the good, and my forefathers who came before me have taken it." Allah revealed to him: "They were tested with trials that you have not been tested with, and they endured them. Ibrahim was tested with Nimrod and with the sacrifice of his son, and Ishaq [[It has already been mentioned that the one sacrificed was Isma'il, peace be upon him.]] was tested with being sacrificed and with the loss of his sight, and Ya'qub was tested with grief over Yusuf (Joseph)." He said: "O Lord, if You had tested me with the same as You tested them, I would also have endured." Allah revealed to him: "You will be tested in such-and-such a month, on such-and-such a day, so be on your guard." When that day that Allah had promised him came, Dawud entered his mihrab (prayer chamber) and closed its door, and began to pray and recite the Zabur (Psalms). While he was in that state, Satan came to him, having taken the form of a golden dove, with every beautiful colour in it. It is said: Its two wings were of pearl and chrysolite. It fell between his feet, and its beauty pleased him. He stretched out his hand to take it, intending to show it to the Children of Israel so that they would look at the power of Allah, the Exalted. When he meant to take it, it flew off, not far away, without letting him despair of it. He reached out to take it, and it moved aside. He followed it, and it flew until it settled in a window opening. He went to take it, and it flew out of the window. Dawud looked to see where it would land, so that he could send someone to catch it. Then he saw a woman in a garden, beside the edge of a pool of hers, bathing. This is the saying of al-Kalbi. [[These reports are weak. See what al-Suyuti quoted from Ibn Hajar in al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/700–701.]]

Al-Suddi said: He saw her bathing on her roof. He saw a woman of the most beautiful of women in form, and Dawud marvelled at her beauty. She turned and glanced, and saw his shadow, so she unbound her hair and covered her body with it. This increased his admiration for her, so he asked about her. It was said: She is Tayshai' daughter of Shaya', the wife of Uriyya ibn Hanana, and her husband was on a military campaign at al-Balqa' with Ayyub ibn Suriya, the son of Dawud's sister.

Some of them mentioned that he desired to have Uriyya killed so that he could marry his wife, and that this was the extent of his sin.

Some of them mentioned that Dawud wrote to his nephew Ayyub: "Send Uriyya to such-and-such a place, and put him in front of the Ark (al-Tabut). Whoever is put in front of the Ark may not turn back behind it until Allah grants victory through his hands or he is martyred." So he sent him and put him in front, and victory was granted through him. He wrote to Dawud about that, and Dawud wrote to him again to send him against the enemy of such-and-such. He sent him, and victory was granted through him. He wrote to Dawud about that, and Dawud wrote to him again to send him against an enemy of such-and-such, who was mightier in valour. He sent him, and he was killed in the third campaign. When the woman's waiting period (iddah) ended, Dawud married her, and she is the mother of Sulayman (Solomon), peace be upon them both. [[See al-Tabari: 23/147.]]

It is reported from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "Dawud's sin was that he asked a man to give up his wife to him."

The people of tafsir said: That was permissible for them, but Allah, the Exalted, did not approve of it for him, because he was one who had a desire for worldly things and a great increase in wives, and Allah had made him independent of her through what He had given him of others.

It is reported from al-Hasan concerning the cause of the trial of Dawud, peace be upon him: He had divided time into portions: a day for his wives, a day for worship, a day for judging among the Children of Israel, and a day for the Children of Israel, when he would discuss with them, they would discuss with him, and he would make them weep and they would make him weep. When it came to the day of the Children of Israel, they reminded him and said: "Does there come upon a man a day in which he does not commit a sin?" Dawud then concealed in himself that he would be able to manage that. [[Reported by al-Tabari: 23/148, and al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/158–159 also attributed it to Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir.]]

It is also said: They mentioned the temptation of women, and Dawud concealed in himself that if he were tested, he would be protected. When it was the day of his worship, he closed his doors and commanded that no one enter upon him, and he devoted himself to the Torah (al-Tawrah). While he was reading, a golden dove came to him, as we have mentioned. He said: Uriyya's wife had been sent by him with one of his armies, and he had written to him to march to such-and-such a place, where, if he marched, he would be killed. He did so, and was struck down, and he married his wife.

They said: When Dawud took Uriyya's wife, he did not remain long before Allah sent to him two angels in the form of two men, on his day of worship. They asked to enter upon him, but the guards prevented them, so they climbed over the mihrab to him. He did not notice, while he was praying, until they were sitting before him. It is said they were Jibril (Gabriel) and Mika'il (Michael). This is the meaning of His saying, Exalted and Majestic: ﴿Has the news of the adversaries reached you?﴾, meaning the account of the adversaries, ﴿when they climbed over the prayer chamber﴾, meaning they ascended and went up. It is said: "Tasawwartu al-hA'it wa al-sur" when you climb over a wall or a rampart. The verb is in the plural, though they are two, because khasm (adversary) is a noun that applies to the singular, the dual, the plural, the masculine and the feminine, and the sense of plurality exists in two, because the sense of plurality is the joining of one thing to another. This is as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿For your hearts have indeed inclined﴾ [al-Tahrim: 4].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 38, verse 22–23:

﴿When they entered upon Dawud, and he was alarmed by them﴾ He feared them when they burst in upon him in his prayer niche (mihrab) without his permission. So he said: "What has brought you in to me?" ﴿They said: "Fear not. Two litigants [i.e., we are two litigants]﴾ [[What is between the brackets is an addition from "b".]] ﴿one of us has wronged the other﴾: we have come to you so that you may judge between us. If it is asked: how could they say "one of us has wronged the other" when they were two angels who do not wrong? It is answered: its meaning is, "Consider two litigants, one of whom has wronged the other." This is one of the indirect forms of speech (ma'arid al-kalam), not a definite assertion that one of them had committed wrong.

﴿So judge between us with truth, and do not exceed the bounds﴾ i.e., do not deviate. It is said: "shaṭṭa al-rajulu shaṭaṭan wa ashaṭṭa ishṭaṭan" (shaṭṭa al-rajulu shaṭaṭan wa ashaṭṭa ishṭaṭan [[In A: shaṭāṭan.]]), meaning he acted unjustly in his judgment. Its meaning is transgressing the limit. The root of the word is from "shaṭṭat al-dar wa ashaṭṭat," meaning it became distant. ﴿And guide us to the even path﴾ i.e., guide us to the way of rightness and justice. Then Dawud said to them: "Speak."

One of them said: ﴿Indeed, this is my brother﴾ i.e., upon my religion and way. ﴿He has ninety-nine ewes﴾ [meaning women] ﴿and I have one ewe﴾ i.e., one woman. The Arabs use "ewe" as a metaphor for a woman. [[See "al-Isra'iliyyat wal-Mawdu'at fi Kutub al-Tafsir" by Abu Shahba, pp. (266–270).]] Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: this is an indirect allusion for the purpose of alerting and making understood, since there were no ewes and no wronging there; it is like their saying: "Zayd struck ʿAmr," or "Bakr bought a house," when there was no striking or buying there.

﴿So he said: "Entrust her to me"﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: give her to me. Mujahid said: step down for me from her. Its real meaning is: include her with me, make me her guardian (kafil), that is, the one who supports her and spends on her. The meaning is: divorce her so that I may marry her. ﴿And he has overpowered me in speech﴾ i.e., he has defeated me in the word. It is also said: he subdued me by the strength of his kingship. Al-Dahhak said: if he speaks, he is more eloquent than I, and if he fights, he is mightier than I. The real meaning is that the victory was his because of my weakness in his hand, even though the right was with me. All of this is a parable for the matter of Dawud with Uriyya, the husband of the woman whom Dawud married, since Dawud had ninety-nine wives and Uriyya had one wife, so he included her with his wives.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 38, verse 24:**

﴿[He] said﴾ Dawud: ﴿"He has certainly wronged you by demanding your ewe to add to his ewes."﴾ That is, by his demanding your ewe so that he might add it to his ewes.

If it is asked: how could he say "He has certainly wronged you" when he had not heard the words of the other party?

It is answered: its meaning is, "If the matter is as you say, then he has wronged you." It is also said: he said this after the other party had acknowledged what he was saying.

﴿"And indeed many of the partners [khulata' (associates who share property)]"﴾ — the associates — ﴿"wrong one another, except those who believe and do righteous deeds"﴾, for they do not wrong anyone.

﴿"And few are they"﴾: that is, they are few, and "ma" is extra (sila). That is, the righteous who do not wrong others are few.

They said: when Dawud had judged between them, one of them looked at his companion and laughed, and ascended to the sky. Dawud then knew that God the Exalted had tested him. This is His saying:

﴿"And Dawud realised [zanna (thought/supposed)]"﴾ — he became certain and knew — ﴿"that We had tried him"﴾, that We had tested him.

Al-Suddi, with his chain of narration, said: when one of them said, "This is my brother," and the rest of the verse, Dawud said to the other, "What do you say?" He replied: "I have ninety-nine ewes, and my brother has one ewe, and I want to take it from him so that my ewes become a hundred." He said: "He was unwilling." [Dawud said:] "Then we will not leave you alone, and if you attempt that I will strike this and this and this from you," meaning: the tip of the nose, its base, and the forehead. The man said: "O Dawud, you are more deserving of this, since Uriyya had only one wife, while you have ninety-nine wives." And he kept exposing him to death until he was killed, and you married his wife. Dawud looked around and saw no one, and so he understood what he had fallen into [[See al-Tabari: 23/147.]].

Those who uphold the freedom of the prophets from sin in this story say: the sin of Dawud was only that he wished the wife of Uriyya were lawful for him. Then it happened that Uriyya went to war, advanced in battle, and was killed. When news of his death reached Dawud, he did not grieve for him as he would have grieved for another of his soldiers who died. Then he married his wife. God therefore rebuked him for this, because the sins of the prophets, though small, are great in the sight of God.

It is also said: the sin of Dawud was that Uriyya had proposed to that woman and had resolved to marry her. When he was away on his military campaign, Dawud proposed to her, and she married him because of his high station. Uriyya was saddened by this, and God rebuked him for it, because he did not leave this one woman to her suitor when he already had ninety-nine wives.

Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us, saying: Among the things that confirm what we have mentioned from the earlier scholars is what Aqil ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Faqih informed me: that al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya al-Qadi in Baghdad informed him, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari, who said: Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la al-Sayrafi narrated to me, [he said:] Ibn Wahb informed us, Ibn Lahi'a informed me, on the authority of Abu Sakhr, on the authority of Yazid al-Raqashi, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him), that he heard him say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When Dawud the Prophet (peace be upon him) looked at the woman and resolved to take her, [and] he instructed the commander of the expedition, saying, 'When the enemy is present, put so-and-so forward before the Ark.' The Ark, in that time, was used to seek victory, and [whoever was] placed before the Ark would not retreat until he was killed or the army fled from him. So the woman's husband was killed. Then the two angels descended to recount his story to him. Dawud perceived [the matter], so he prostrated and remained prostrate for forty nights, until the crops grew from his tears on his head, and the earth consumed [the moisture] from his forehead. In his prostration he said: 'My Lord, Dawud has slipped in a slip further away than the distance between east and west. My Lord, if You do not have mercy on the weakness of Dawud and forgive his sin, You will make his sin a tale among the creatures after him.' Then Gabriel came to him after forty nights and said: 'O Dawud, Allah has forgiven you the concern you had.' Dawud said: 'My Lord is able to forgive me the concern I had, and I know that Allah is just and does not incline. So what of so-and-so when he comes on the Day of Resurrection?' [The man] said: 'O Lord, my blood is with Dawud.' Gabriel said: 'I did not ask your Lord about that, but if you wish I will do it.' He said: 'Yes.' So Gabriel ascended, and Dawud prostrated, and he remained as long as Allah willed. Then Gabriel descended and said: 'I asked Allah, O Dawud, about that for which you sent me, and He said: Tell Dawud that Allah will gather you both on the Day of Resurrection, and He will say to him, "Give Me your blood that is with Dawud," and he will say, "It is yours, O Lord." Then He will say: "Indeed you will have in Paradise whatever you wish and desire as recompense for it."'" [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 23/150–151. al-Suyuti attributed it to al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Abi Hatim with a weak chain, in which Yazid al-Raqashi is weak, and Ibn Lahi'a became confused. See also Ibn Kathir's Tafsir: 4/32, and Abu Shahba's al-Isra'iliyyat wa al-Mawdu'at: pp. 265–268.]]

It is related from Ibn Abbas, Ka'b al-Ahbar, and Wahb ibn Munabbih, all of whom said: When the two angels came to Dawud and he passed judgement against himself, they changed their forms and ascended while saying, "The man has passed judgement against himself." Dawud knew that this was what was meant, so he fell down prostrate for forty days, lifting his head only for a need or for the time of an obligatory prayer, then returning to prostration for a full forty days. He neither ate nor drank, while weeping, until grass grew around his head, and he called upon his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, asking Him for repentance. Among his supplications in prostration were: "Glory be to the Great King, who tests creation with what He wills. Glory be to the Creator of light. Glory be to the One who comes between hearts. Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, You left me alone with my enemy, Iblis, and I did not stand firm against his temptation when it descended upon me. Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, You created me, and from Your prior knowledge is what I am heading towards. Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, woe to Dawud when the veil is lifted from him, and it is said, 'This is Dawud the sinner.' Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, with what eye shall I look upon You on the Day of Resurrection, when the wrongdoers look only with a furtive glance? [Glory be to the Creator of light] [[Omitted from "a".]] My God, with what foot shall I walk before You and stand before You on the day when the feet of sinners slip? Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, from where does the servant seek forgiveness except from his master? Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, I cannot bear the heat of Your sun, so how can I bear the heat of Your Fire? Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, I cannot bear the sound of Your thunder, so how can I bear the whip of Hell? Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, woe to Dawud because of the great sin he committed. Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, You know my secret and my open [deeds], so accept my excuse. Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, by Your mercy forgive my sins, and do not distance me from Your mercy because of my desires. Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, I seek refuge in the light of Your noble Face from my sins that have destroyed me. Glory be to the Creator of light. I have fled to You with my sins, and I have acknowledged my wrongdoing, so do not make me among the despairing, and do not disgrace me on the Day of Judgement. Glory be to the Creator of light." [[There is nothing in the noble verses of this kind of narration, nor in any of the reliable books of hadith, which are the ones relied upon.]]

Mujahid said: He remained prostrate for forty days, not lifting his head, until pasture grew from the tears of his eyes, until it covered his head. Then he was called: "O Dawud, are you hungry so that you may be fed? Or thirsty so that you may be given drink? Or naked so that you may be clothed?" And I answer in a manner other than what he asked. He said: So he gave a great sob, by which the wood was set aflame and burned from the heat of his inner being. Then Allah sent down repentance and forgiveness for him [[See al-Tabari: 23/150.]].

Wahb said: A call came to Dawud: "I have indeed forgiven you." He said: "My Lord, how [can it be], when You do not wrong anyone?" He said: "Go to the grave of Uriyya and call out to him, for I will let him hear your call, and you will be absolved by him." So he went, wearing woollen garments, until he sat at his grave. Then he called out, "O Uriyya!" He replied, "Here I am. Who is this who has cut off my pleasure and woken me?" He said: "I am Dawud." He said: "What has brought you, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "I ask you to release me from what I did to you." He said: "And what did you do to me?" He said: "I exposed you to death." He said: "You exposed me to Paradise, so you are absolved." Then Allah revealed to him: "O Dawud, did you not know that I am a just judge who does not decide by harshness? Did you not inform him that you had married his wife?" He said: So he returned to him, called him, and he answered, saying: "Who is this who has interrupted my pleasure?" He said: "I am Dawud." He said: "O Prophet of Allah, have I not already pardoned you?" He said: "Yes, but I only did that to you because of your wife, and I have married her." He said: So [Uriyya] was silent and did not answer him. He called him again, and he did not answer. He called him a third time, and he did not answer. So [Dawud] stood by his grave and put dust on his head, then called out: "Woe to Dawud, then a long woe to Dawud! Glory be to the Creator of light. Woe to Dawud when the scales are set up with justice. Glory be to the Creator of light. Woe, then a long woe to him, when he is seized by his chin and handed over to the one who was wronged. Glory be to the Creator of light. Woe, then a long woe to him, when he is dragged on his face with the sinners into the Fire. Glory be to the Creator of light." Then a call came to him from heaven: "O Dawud, I have forgiven your sin, had mercy on your weeping, answered your supplication, and removed your stumble." He said: "My Lord, how [can it be], when my companion has not pardoned me?" He said: "O Dawud, on the Day of Resurrection I will give him from the reward what no eye has seen and no ear has heard. Then I will say to him, 'Are you pleased, My servant?' He will say, 'My Lord, from where is this for me, when my deeds have not reached it?' I will say, 'This is in exchange for My servant Dawud, and I will ask you to give it to Me, and you will give it to Me.'" He said: "My Lord, now I know that You have forgiven me" [[See al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/160–161.]].

This is the saying of God the Exalted:

﴿"So he sought forgiveness from his Lord and fell down bowing [rak'an]"﴾, that is, prostrating. He expressed prostration by "bowing" because each of them involves bending.

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: Abdullah ibn Tahir asked me about His saying, "and fell down bowing": Is "fell down" said of one who is bowing? I said: No, and its meaning is: he fell down after he had been bowing, that is, he prostrated. ﴿"And he turned penitently [anaba]"﴾, that is, he returned and repented.

﴿So We forgave him that﴾, meaning that sin. ﴿And indeed he has with Us﴾, after the forgiveness, ﴿on the Day of Resurrection, a station of nearness﴾, meaning closeness and status, ﴿and a good place of return﴾, meaning a good place of return and final abode.

Wahb ibn Munabbih [[The report of Wahb is also one of the Isra'iliyyat (narratives from Jewish and Christian sources) in this story, as mentioned earlier.]] said: When Dawud (David) repented, Allah accepted his repentance, and he wept over his sin for thirty years. His tears did not dry up, night or day. He had committed the sin when he was seventy years old. After the sin, he divided his time into four days: one day for judging between the Children of Israel, one day for his wives, one day for travelling through the deserts, mountains and shores, and one day for seclusion in a house he had, which contained four thousand prayer niches (mihrab). The monks would gather to him there, and he would lament over himself with them, and they would help him in that. When it was the day of his lamentation, he would go out to the deserts, raise his voice with the Psalms (al-mazamir), and weep, and the trees, sand, birds and wild animals would weep with him, until their tears flowed like rivers. Then he would come to the mountains, raise his voice with the Psalms, and weep, and the mountains, stones, beasts and birds would weep with him, until the valleys flowed with their weeping. Then he would come to the shore, raise his voice with the Psalms, and weep, and the fish, sea creatures, water birds and predators would weep with him. When evening came, he would return. When it was the day of his lamentation over himself, his caller would announce: "Today is the day of Dawud's lamentation over himself; let whoever will help him attend." He would enter the house containing the prayer niches, and three woollen mats (musuh) stuffed with palm fibre would be spread for him. He would sit on them, and four thousand monks would come, wearing hooded cloaks (baranis) and holding staves. They would sit in those niches, and then Dawud would raise his voice in weeping and lamentation over himself, and the monks would raise their voices with him. He would keep weeping until the mats were soaked with his tears, and Dawud would fall onto them like a fledgling flapping. His son Sulayman would come and lift him up. Dawud would take some of those tears in his palms, wipe his face with them, and say: "O Lord, forgive me for what You see." If the weeping of Dawud were weighed against the weeping of all the people of the world, his would outweigh it.

Wahb also said: Dawud did not raise his head until the angel said to him: "The beginning of your affair was a sin, and its end was disobedience. Raise your head." So he raised his head, and he lived the rest of his life never drinking water without mixing it with his tears, and never eating food without moistening it with his tears.

Al-Awza'i reported with a marfu' chain to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "The eyes of Dawud are like two water-skins pouring water, and his tears have carved channels in his face like the channels of water in the earth" [[Weak. Narrated by Imam Ahmad in al-Zuhd, and by al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi in Nawadir al-Usul. See al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/163.]].

Wahb said: When Allah accepted the repentance of Dawud, he said: "O Lord, You have forgiven me. But how can I not forget my sin, so that I may seek forgiveness for it, and for the sinners until the Day of Resurrection?" He said: So Allah marked his sin on his right hand. He never lifted food or drink to it without weeping when he saw it. Whenever he stood to address the people, he would spread out his palm and face the people so that they could see the mark of his sin. And when he supplicated, he would begin by asking forgiveness for the sinners before himself.

Qatadah reported from al-Hasan: After the sin, Dawud would sit only with sinners, saying: "Come to Dawud the sinner." He would not drink any drink without mixing it with the tears of his eyes. He would place dry barley bread in a bowl and keep weeping over it until it was moistened with the tears of his eyes. He would sprinkle salt and ashes on it and eat, saying: "This is the food of sinners." He said: Before the sin, Dawud would stand in prayer for half the night and fast for half the year. After what happened in his sin, he fasted the whole year and stood in prayer the whole night.

Thabit said: When Dawud remembered the punishment of Allah, his joints would come apart, and only the Lord's binding would hold them together again; and when he remembered the mercy of Allah, they would return to their place.

In the story it is also said that the wild beasts and birds used to listen to his recitation, but after he did what he did, they no longer paid attention to his recitation. It is narrated that they said: "O Dawud, your sin has departed with the sweetness of your voice" [[Qadi Iyad said in his book al-Shifa bi-Ta'rif Huquq al-Mustafa, 2/827–828: "Do not turn to what the transmitters from the People of the Book have written, those who altered and changed, and which the exegetes have related. Allah the Exalted has not specified anything of that in His Book, nor has it come in a sound hadith. What Allah has specified in the story of Dawud is His saying: 'And Dawud thought that We had only tested him' (38:24). There is no established report in the story of Dawud and Uriah." Al-Dawudi said: "There is no established report in the story of Dawud and Uriah, and one should not attribute to a prophet the desire to kill a Muslim."]].

And ‘Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, who said: Ahmad ibn ‘Abd Allah al-Nu‘aymi informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Isma‘il (al-Bukhari) narrated to us, who said: Sulayman ibn Harb and Abu al-Nu‘man narrated to us, both saying: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ayyub, from ‘Ikrimah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "The prostration of Sad is not one of the obligatory prostrations, though I have seen the Prophet ﷺ prostrate in it" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the chapter on prostrations of the Qur'an, chapter: The prostration of (Sad), 2/553.]].

And ‘Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, who said: Ahmad ibn ‘Abd Allah al-Nu‘aymi informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Isma‘il (al-Bukhari) narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn ‘Ubayd al-Tanafisi narrated to us, from al-‘Awwam, who said: I asked Mujahid about the prostration of Sad, and he said: I asked Ibn ‘Abbas, "From where did you prostrate?" He said: "Do you not recite: 'And among his descendants, Dawud and Sulayman…' until 'Those are the ones whom Allah guided, so follow their guidance' (6:84–90)? And Dawud was among those whom your Prophet was commanded to follow. So Dawud prostrated for it, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prostrated for it."  [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the commentary, the commentary of Surah (Sad), 8/544.]]

Abu ‘Uthman Sa‘id ibn Isma‘il al-Dabbi informed us, who said: Abu Muhammad ‘Abd al-Jabbar ibn Muhammad al-Jarrahi informed us, who said: Abu al-‘Abbas Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mahbubi narrated to us, who said: Abu ‘Isa al-Tirmidhi narrated to us, who said: Qutaybah narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn Khunays narrated to us, who said: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Yazid narrated to us, who said: Ibn Jurayj said to me: ‘Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Yazid informed me, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I saw myself last night in a dream, as if I were praying behind a tree. I prostrated, and the tree prostrated for my prostration. I heard it saying: O Allah, record for me with You a reward through it, remove from me through it a burden, make it for me with You a treasure, and accept it from me as You accepted it from Your servant Dawud.'" Al-Hasan said: Ibn Jurayj said: "Your grandfather said to me": Ibn ‘Abbas said: So the Prophet ﷺ recited a prostration and then prostrated, and I heard him saying [the like of that] [[Omitted from manuscript "b".]] what the man had reported about the saying of the tree" [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in the Friday chapters, the chapters on travel, chapter: What is said in the prostration of the Qur'an, 3/181. Abu ‘Isa said: "This is a strange hadith from Ibn ‘Abbas; we know it only through this route." Also narrated by Ibn Majah in the chapter on establishing prayer and its Sunnah, chapter: Prostration of the Qur'an, no. 1053, 1/334; and al-Hakim, 1/219–220, who authenticated it and was agreed with by al-Dhahabi. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Talkhis, 2/8: "al-Shafi‘i narrated it in al-Umm from Ibn ‘Uyaynah, from Ayyub, from ‘Ikrimah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, as a marfu‘ report. He narrated it in al-Qadim from Sufyan, from ‘Umar ibn Dharr, from his father, who said: 'Dawud prostrated for it.' Al-Bayhaqi said: It is also narrated by another route from ‘Umar ibn Dharr, from his father, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ‘Abbas, as a continuous chain, but it is not strong." I say (Ibn Hajar): al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Hajjaj ibn Muhammad, from ‘Umar ibn Dharr, as a continuous chain; al-Daraqutni narrated it from the hadith of ‘Abd Allah ibn Bazi‘ from ‘Umar ibn Dharr in similar wording, and Ibn al-Jawzi criticised it on that basis, but it has been supported by another route, and Ibn al-Sakan authenticated it. In al-Bukhari, from ‘Ikrimah, from Ibn ‘Abbas: (Sad) is not one of the obligatory prostrations, though I have seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prostrate in it." See also: Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Sahihah, no. 2710.]]

The Lord's saying, ﴿O David, indeed We have made you a khalifah (vicegerent) upon the earth﴾, meaning: you manage the affairs of the servants by Our command. ﴿So judge between the people with truth﴾, meaning: with justice. ﴿And do not follow desire, for it will lead you astray from the path of Allah. Indeed, those who go astray from the path of Allah will have a severe punishment for having forgotten the Day of Reckoning﴾, meaning: because they abandoned belief in the Day of Reckoning. Al-Zajjaj said: "By their abandoning action for that Day."

Ikrimah and al-Suddi said: In the verse there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir). Its sense is: "For them is a severe punishment on the Day of Reckoning, because they forgot," meaning: they abandoned judging with justice.

﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain﴾. Ibn Abbas said: Not for reward and not for punishment.

﴿That is the assumption of those who disbelieve﴾, meaning: the people of Makkah, who assumed that they were created for nothing, and that there is no resurrection and no reckoning. ﴿So woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 38, verses 29–31:

﴿A Book We have sent down to you﴾, meaning: this Book We have sent down to you. ﴿Blessed﴾, its good and benefit are abundant. ﴿That they may ponder﴾, meaning: that they may reflect upon ﴿its verses﴾, and that they may contemplate them. Abu Ja'far (one of the Qur'anic reciters) read "*littadabbaru*" with a single *ta'* and a lightened *dal*. Al-Hasan said: "Tadabbur of its verses is following it." ﴿And that those of understanding may be mindful﴾, meaning: that they may be admonished.

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And We gave to Dawud, Sulayman. How excellent a servant he was! Indeed, he was ever turning back (to Allah). When there were displayed before him, at evening, the well-bred steeds of the *ṣāffināt* [standing on three legs]﴾.

Al-Kalbi said: Sulayman raided the people of Damascus and Nasibin, and he took from them a thousand horses.

The Qur'anic phrase ﴿And We certainly tested Solomon﴾: We tested him and afflicted him by stripping him of his kingdom.

The cause of this was what Muhammad ibn Ishaq reported from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: Solomon, peace be upon him, heard of a city on one of the islands of the sea called Sayda (Sidon), which had a king of great standing. People could not reach him because of his location in the sea. God had given Solomon, in his kingdom, an authority by which nothing on land or sea could resist him. He would ride the wind wherever he wished. He set out toward that city, carried by the wind over the surface of the water, until he landed there with his armies of jinn and humans. He killed its king, seized control of it, took its booty, and took its people captive. Among what he obtained was a daughter of that king called Jarada, whose beauty and loveliness had no equal. He chose her for himself and invited her to Islam. She accepted Islam, though with some coldness and little understanding. He loved her with a love he had not given to any of his other wives. But she remained in such grief that her sorrow never left her and her tears never dried. This troubled Solomon, and he said to her: "Woe to you! What is this grief that does not leave you, and this weeping that does not dry?" She said: "I remember my father, and I remember his kingdom, what was in it, and what befell him, and that saddens me." Solomon said: "God has replaced him for you with a kingdom greater than his kingdom, and an authority greater than his authority, and He has guided you to Islam, which is better than all of that." She said: "That is so, but whenever I remember him, I am afflicted with the grief you see. If you were to order the devils to fashion his likeness in my house, where I live, so that I might see it morning and evening, I would hope that this would remove my grief and console me for some of what I feel within myself."

So Solomon commanded the devils and said: "Make for her the likeness of her father in her house, so that she will not find anything strange in him." They fashioned it for her until she looked upon her father as he was, except that there was no spirit in it. She went to it when they had made it, dressed it in a waist-wrapper, a shirt, and a turban, and clothed it in garments like those he used to wear. Then, whenever Solomon left her house, she would go out to it with her attendants and prostrate herself before it, and they would prostrate before it as they used to do before him in his kingdom. Each evening she would do the same. Solomon knew nothing of any of this for forty mornings.

The news reached Asif ibn Barkhiya, who was a righteous man (siddiq). He was never refused entry at Solomon's doors. At any hour he wished to enter any of his houses, he would enter, whether Solomon was present or absent. He came to him and said: "O Prophet of God, my years have grown great, my bones have grown frail, my life has run out, and the time of my departure has come. I wish to stand in a place before death where I may mention the prophets of God who have passed, praise them with my knowledge of them, and teach the people some of what they were ignorant of concerning many of their affairs." Solomon said: "Do so." So he gathered the people for him, and he stood among them to preach. He mentioned the prophets of God, may He be exalted, and praised each prophet for what was in him. He mentioned what God had favoured them with, until he reached Solomon, and said: "How gentle you were in your youth! How scrupulous you were in your youth! How excellent you were in your youth! How firm your affairs were in your youth! How far you were from everything you disliked in your youth!" Then he left.

Solomon, peace be upon him, felt something within himself because of this, to the point that he was filled with anger. When Solomon entered his house, he sent for him and said: "O Asif, you mentioned the prophets of God who have passed, and you praised them in every age and in every condition of theirs. But when you mentioned me, you began praising me for my youth, and you were silent about all else concerning my affairs in my old age. What have I done at the end of my affairs?" Asif said: "Other than God has been worshipped in your house for forty mornings, for the sake of a woman's desire." Solomon said: "In my house?" He said: "In your house." Solomon said: "We belong to God, and to Him we return. I know that you only said what you said because of something that reached you." Then Solomon returned to his house, broke that idol, and punished that woman and her attendants.

Then he commanded that garments of purity be brought to him. They were garments that were spun only by virgins, woven only by virgins, and washed only by virgins, and no woman who had seen blood had touched them. He put them on and went out alone into a barren tract of land. He commanded that ashes be spread for him, and then he came, repentant to God, may He be exalted, until he sat upon those ashes and rolled in them in his garments, humbling himself before God, may He be exalted, and beseeching Him, weeping and calling out, and seeking forgiveness for what had happened in his house. He remained in this state all that day until evening. Then he returned to his house.

He had an umm walad (a slave-mother, a concubine who had borne a child to her master) called al-Amina. Whenever he entered the place where he relieved himself, or wished to be intimate with one of his wives, he would place his ring with her until he had purified himself. He never touched his ring except when he was in a state of purity. His kingdom was in his ring. One day he placed it with her, then entered his place for relieving himself. The devil of the sea, called Sakhr, came to her in the form of Solomon, so that she found nothing strange in him, and said: "My ring, Amina!" She handed it to him, and he put it on his hand. Then he went out and sat on the throne of Solomon. The birds, the jinn, and the humans gathered around him. Solomon came out and went to Amina, but his condition and appearance had changed in the eyes of everyone who saw him. He said: "O Amina, my ring!" She said: "Who are you?" He said: "I am Solomon ibn Dawud." She said: "You are lying! Solomon has come and taken his ring while he was sitting on the throne of his kingdom." Solomon realised that his sin had overtaken him. He went out and began standing at the houses of the Children of Israel, saying: "I am Solomon ibn Dawud." They threw dust at him and abused him, saying: "Look at this madman, what is he saying! He claims to be Solomon!" When Solomon saw this, he went to the sea, where he began carrying the fish of the sea's people to the market. They gave him two fish each day. When evening came, he would sell one of his two fish for loaves of bread and roast the other and eat it. He remained in this state for forty mornings, equal to the number of days the idol had been worshipped in his house.

Asif and the leaders of the Children of Israel denounced the judgement of the enemy of God, the devil, during those forty days. Asif said: "O assembly of the Children of Israel, have you seen the inconsistency in the judgement of the son of Dawud as I have seen it?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Give me time to enter upon his wives and ask them whether they noticed in his private affairs what we noticed in his public affairs and his conduct." He went in to his wives and said: "Woe to you! Have you noticed in the affairs of the son of Dawud what we have noticed?" They said: "Worst of all, he does not leave any of us women alone in her menstrual blood, and he does not wash from sexual impurity." He said: "We belong to God, and to Him we return. This is truly a manifest trial." Then he went out to the Children of Israel and said: "What is in private is no greater than what is in public." When forty mornings had passed, the devil flew from his seat, passed over the sea, and threw the ring into it. A fish swallowed it, and some fishermen caught the fish. Solomon had worked for them all that day, and when evening came, they gave him his two fish and the fish that had swallowed the ring. Solomon went out with his two fish, and sold the one in whose belly there was no ring for loaves of bread. Then he turned to the other fish and split it open to roast it, and there in its belly he found his ring. He took it and put it on his hand, then fell prostrate. The birds and the jinn gathered around him, and the people came to him. He recognised the one who had entered upon him because of what had happened in his house. He returned to his kingdom and declared his repentance for his sin. Then he commanded the devils, saying: "Bring me Sakhr." The devils searched for him until they seized him and brought him. They also brought him a rock, and he hollowed it out and put him inside it, then sealed it with another rock, bound it with iron and lead, and then commanded that it be thrown into the sea. This is the narration of Wahb.

Al-Hasan said: God would not have given the devil power over his wives.

Al-Suddi said: The cause of Solomon's trial was that he had a hundred wives. One of them, called Jarada, was the one he favoured most and the one he trusted most. Whenever he went to relieve himself, he entrusted his ring to her. One day she said to him: "My brother had a dispute with a certain man, and I would like you to decide in his favour when he comes to you." He said: "Yes," but he did not do it. He was then tested by his own words. He gave her his ring and entered the place for relieving himself. The devil came in his form, took the ring, and sat in Solomon's seat. Solomon came out and asked her for his ring. She said: "Did you not take it?" He said: "No." He went out in his place, and the devil remained judging among the people for forty days. The people denounced his judgement. The reciters and scholars of the Children of Israel gathered and went in to his wives and said: "We have denounced this. If this is Solomon, then his mind has gone." The women wept at that, and the men gathered around him and surrounded him, and they unrolled the Torah and read from it. Then the devil flew from before them until he alighted on a balcony, with the ring still with him. Then he flew until he reached the sea, and the ring fell from him into the sea. A fish swallowed it. Solomon came until he reached a fisherman of the sea, who was hungry and whose hunger had grown severe. He asked him for food from his catch, and said: "I am Solomon." One of them stood up and struck him with a stick, wounding his head. He began washing his blood on the sea shore. The fishermen blamed their companion who had struck him, and they gave him two fish that had gone bad among them. The "exalted assembly" means the angels. ﴿When they disputed﴾ means concerning the matter of Adam, peace be upon him, when Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, I will create upon the earth a successive authority﴾ and they said: ﴿Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein?﴾ (al-Baqarah: 30).

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us: Abu Mansur al-Sam'ani informed us: Abu Ja'far al-Rayyani narrated to us: Humayd ibn Zanjawayh narrated to us: Hisham ibn Ammar narrated to us: Sadaqah ibn Khalid narrated to us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir narrated to us, who said: Khalid ibn al-Lajlaj passed by us, and Makhul called him and said: "O Ibrahim, narrate to us the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn A'idh." He said: I heard Abd al-Rahman ibn A'idh al-Hadrami say: The Prophet ﷺ said: "I saw my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, in the best of forms. He said: 'Concerning what do the exalted assembly dispute, O Muhammad?' I said: 'You know best, my Lord,' twice. He said: Then He placed His palm between my shoulders, and I found its coolness between my breasts, and I knew what is in the heavens and the earth." He said: Then he recited this verse: ﴿And thus We showed Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth that he might be among the certain﴾ (al-An'am: 75). Then He said: "Concerning what do the exalted assembly dispute, O Muhammad?" I said: "Concerning the expiations (kaffarat)." He said: "And what are they?" I said: "Walking on foot to the congregations, sitting in the mosques after the prayers, and completing the ablution in difficult conditions." He said: "Whoever does that will live well, die well, and will be free from his sins as on the day his mother bore him. And among the degrees: feeding others, spreading the greeting of peace, and standing in prayer at night while people are asleep." He said: "Say: O Allah, I ask You for good things, and for abandoning evil deeds, and for love of the poor, and that You forgive me, have mercy on me, and accept my repentance; and when You intend a trial for a people, take me to Yourself without being tested." Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 38, verse 71–81:

The Exalted said: ﴿When your Lord said to the angels, "I am going to create a human being from clay."﴾ He means Adam, peace be upon him.

﴿So when I have proportioned him﴾ — I have perfected his creation — ﴿and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down before him in prostration.﴾ ﴿So the angels prostrated, all of them entirely, except Iblis; he was arrogant and was among the disbelievers. He said, "O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to that which I created with My hands? Are you arrogant?"﴾ The alif is an interrogative alif (alif al-istifham, the alif of questioning) that has entered upon the alif of connection (alif al-wasl, the alif used to connect speech, which is pronounced at the start of a word when it is not preceded by another word), ﴿or were you among the haughty?﴾ — the arrogant. It is an interrogation of rebuke and denial. It means: "Have you become arrogant on your own account, until you refused to prostrate? Or were you among the people who are proud, so you became too proud to prostrate because you were one of them?"

﴿He said, "I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay."﴾ ﴿He said, "Then get out of it,"﴾ that is, out of Paradise. It was also said: out of the heavens. Al-Hasan and Abu al-'Aliyah said: that is, out of the form in which you are. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: this is a sound interpretation, because Iblis acted tyrannically and boasted of his form, so God changed his form, and he became black and ugly after being beautiful. ﴿Indeed, you are accursed﴾ — expelled.

﴿And indeed, upon you is My curse until the Day of Recompense." He said, "My Lord, then reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected." He said, "Indeed, you are among those reprieved until the day of the time well known,"﴾ which is the first blast of the Trumpet.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 38, verses 82–88:

﴿He said, "By Your might, I will surely mislead them all, except Your sincere servants among them."﴾ He said, "So the truth, and the truth I say."﴾ Asim, Hamza and Ya'qub (reciters of the Qur'an) read "fa-al-haqqu" with a raised *qaf* (*raf'*), as the inchoative (*ibtida'*, the subject of a nominal sentence), and its predicate is omitted, its estimated form being: "The truth is from Me." The second *al-haqqa* is in the accusative (*nasb*), meaning: "And I say the truth." This was said by Mujahid. The others read both with the accusative, and they differed about their grammatical function. It was said: the accusative of the first is by way of incitement (*al-ighra'*), as if he said: "Hold fast to the truth," and the second is by way of the verb "to say" governing it, meaning: "I say the truth." It was also said: the first is an oath, meaning: "By the truth," which is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, so it is put in the accusative by removing the preposition [the preposition, and it is] [[Omitted in manuscript "a".]] the letter of description (*harf al-sifah*), and the accusative of the second is by the verb "to say" governing it. It was also said: the second is a repetition of the oath, meaning that Allah swore by Himself.

﴿I will surely fill Hell with you and with whoever follows you of them, all together.﴾ ﴿Say, "I do not ask you for any wage for it"﴾ for conveying the message, ﴿any wage﴾ a reward, ﴿nor am I of those who pretend﴾, those who fabricate the Qur'an from their own opinion. Whoever says something from his own opinion has indeed burdened himself with it.

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Jarir informed us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq who said: We entered upon Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, and he said: "O people, whoever knows something, let him say it, and whoever does not know, let him say: 'Allah knows best,' for it is part of knowledge to say of what one does not know: 'Allah knows best.' Allah, the Exalted, said to His Prophet: ﴿Say, I do not ask you for any wage for it, nor am I of those who pretend.﴾" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, the tafsir of surah Sad, chapter: "Nor am I of those who pretend" 8/547, and by Muslim in the Attributes of the Hypocrites and their Rulings, chapter on smoke, no. 2798, 4/2156–2157.]]

His saying ﴿It is not﴾, meaning: it is not, that is, the Qur'an, ﴿except a reminder﴾, an admonition, ﴿for the worlds﴾, for all of creation.

﴿And you will surely know﴾, you disbelievers of Mecca, ﴿its news﴾, the report of its truth, ﴿after a while﴾. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: after death. Ikrimah said: meaning the Day of Resurrection. Al-Kalbi said: whoever remains will know it when its matter becomes manifest and rises, and whoever dies will know it after his death. Al-Hasan said: "Son of Adam, at death the certain news will come to you."
